device.description: 16-bit 250 kSPS sampling CMOS ADC with internal reference and 16-bit/byte parallel interface
device.note: ads8515.pdf (SLAS460D) p.4-5 specifications (VIH 0.65 VDIG, binary two's complement, VDIG 1.65-5.25 V, bus access/relinquish 83 ns), p.4 pin configuration, p.8 pin descriptions, p.9-10 basic operation, starting a conversion, Table 1 control lines, reading data, Table 2 output codes, p.11 Table 3 conversion timing and Figure 20 BYTE bit locations

commands.name: Convert (CS and R/C low)
commands.note: p.10 Table 1: CS falling with R/C low, or R/C falling with CS low, initiates conversion n (CS and R/C are ORed and level triggered)

pages: p.4-5 (VIH 0.65xVDIG, binary two's complement, VDIG 1.65-5.25 V, bus access / relinquish 83 ns), p.4 (pin configuration), p.8 (pin descriptions: BYTE low = 8 MSBs, high = 8 LSBs; D15-D0 Hi-Z when CS high or R/C low), p.10 (Table 1 control lines; reading data: output active when R/C high and CS low; Table 2: 0 V = 0000h), p.11 (Table 3: tconv 2 us max, ten 30 ns max, tdis 83 ns max; Figure 20: BYTE high swaps the bytes, pins 6-13 = bits 7-0, pins 15-22 = bits 15-8)
notModeled: analog input (+/-10 V), internal 2.5 V reference (REF) and CAP buffer

the conversion starts when the CS/R/C low period ends (write access end) rather than at its falling edge; the 40 ns convert pulse width and the rule that CS or R/C must be high when BUSY rises (else a conversion restarts without acquisition) are not checked
reading during a conversion returns the previous result (valid up to tv after the start); the model keeps the same 0 V code throughout
tAcc uses ten (bus enable 30 ns max, Table 3); ta (data valid after R/C low, 1.2 us) is the conversion data latency and not modeled; BYTE switching delay td4 (30 ns)
